text:
zoe: heads-up: customer on Win11 using conda env (py3.10) reports our async onboarding snippet fails with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED. Sync sample works if they set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE to the corp CA, but async still errors. stack shows ssl.SSLCertVerificationError buried under an httpx ConnectError.

mike: ok. two layers: corporate TLS interception (corp CA) and how async stack discovers cert bundles. requests honors REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE env and conda/python builds often link OpenSSL differently. httpx/anyio may not pick up that env depending on backend.

ali: also note conda ships OpenSSL and might ignore python.org cert handling. i've seen wheels built against OpenSSL 1.1 that behave differently than 3.x. if the cert trust store isn't the same as requests, verification fails.

zoe: customer tried setting SSL_CERT_FILE to the certifi path, and also set REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, then restarted; sync works, async still fails. they said they can't easily change machine policies to add corp CA to Windows store.

mike: reproducible workaround i use locally: create SSLContext using certifi and pass it into AsyncClient, plus switch to selector event loop on Windows:```python
import ssl, certifi, asyncio
from redwood import AsyncClient

ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where())
# keep windows compatibility
try:
    asyncio.set_event_loop_policy(asyncio.WindowsSelectorEventLoopPolicy())
except Exception:
    pass

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(ssl=ctx) as c:
        await c.generate("hi")

asyncio.run(main())
```

mike: that forces the same trust chain as requests. we should ship a one-liner helper in the SDK for Windows/conda users.

ali: SDK API mismatch: sync client accepts `verify` (bool|str) and respects REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE; async path accepts an internal ssl arg in code but stubs don't expose it, so users try verify=... and mypy explodes. we should accept both `verify` and `ssl` for parity and document precedence.

sophie: extra wrinkle: our retry middleware was swallowing the original SSLCertVerificationError. it re-raises a new RequestError without chaining __cause__, so customers only see ConnectError. that makes triage impossible for support.

zoe: agreed — customer pasted logs and support couldn't tell it was a cert problem until they enabled debug logging.

mike: action items i propose: 1) add an AsyncClient param `verify: Optional[Union[bool,str]]` and `ssl: Optional[ssl.SSLContext]` in stubs and runtime, with clear precedence (ssl param > verify path > env vars > certifi fallback on Windows), 2) add helper `redwood.windows_ssl_context()` that returns ssl.create_default_context(cafile=certifi.where()) and document selector loop tip, 3) preserve exception chaining in retry middleware so __cause__ is visible, 4) add a lightweight Windows/conda job to GH Actions matrix for py3.8-3.12.

ali: also suggest a test harness that simulates corporate MITM (mitmproxy or custom cert) in CI so we catch platform-specific cert discovery regressions. and call out conda vs python.org in onboarding docs.

sophie: i'll file the issue and include a minimal repro and the customer's conda details. will attach example logs showing inner SSLCertVerificationError.

devex-bot: Issue 2625 created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/2625 - "windows-conda-corp-ca-async-ssl-parity-typing-ci"

zoe: thanks! if we can get a small patch that ships the helper and exposes verify/ssl in stubs that will unblock the partner. also please add a troubleshooting blurb for corporate proxies and mention upgrading cryptography/openssl. :thumbsup:

mike: i'll open a tiny PR: expose verify/ssl in AsyncClient, add windows_ssl_context helper, preserve exception chaining, and add the CI ticket notes.

ali: one more note: document recommended guidance for enterprise deploys (Private/Dedicated) to configure REDWOOD_SSL_CERT_FILE or plug their KMS/HSM-backed cert store so customers don't have to tweak env vars.

sophie: tagging @platform for the CI matrix change. if approved i'll add the mitmproxy test as an opt-in job to avoid flakiness.

zoe: will update the onboarding issue with the partner repro and next steps. thanks all.
